t: Abd al-Rahman III proclaimed himself caliph at Córdoba in 929, rivalling the Abbasids of Baghdad and the Fatimids.
Córdoba became the largest city of western Europe, with the Great Mosque, Madinat al-Zahra and celebrated libraries.
After the regent Almanzor’s death, civil war from 1009 broke the caliphate, which was abolished in 1031.
dyk: In 958 the deposed King Sancho I of León, known as ‘the Fat’, travelled to Córdoba with his grandmother Queen Toda of Navarre to be treated for obesity by Hasdai ibn Shaprut.
ev: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims himself caliph
Work begins on the palace city of Madinat al-Zahra
Ramiro II of León defeats the caliph at the Battle of Simancas
Al-Hakam II succeeds and later enlarges the Great Mosque of Córdoba
A revolt in Córdoba begins the Fitna, the civil war of al-Andalus
Berber troops take and plunder Córdoba
The notables of Córdoba abolish the caliphate
